modules.responsibility: The initializer exports Bank, BankAccount, CreditCard, and Transaction as the package API for the finance model.
The package initializer marks a Python package and contains no executable domain logic.
Defines finance-owned typed payloads for generated values and serialized account and transaction records.
BankAccountGenerator generates account balances, account types, and dates using its configured RNG and resolved clock.
BankGenerator generates bank records, BIC and BIN identifiers, and customer-service phone numbers from its configured dataset and RNG.
CreditCardGenerator selects card specifications and generates card credentials, status, credit limits, and balances using its configured RNG.

TransactionGenerator generates transaction values and ID candidates, including weighted international status, and anchors transaction time and reference values to the injected RNG and resolved run clock.
The function calculates the Luhn check digit for formatted payment identifiers.
The package initializer marks a Python package and contains no executable domain logic.
Bank exposes cached institution identity, payment-network identifiers, routing data, and customer-service contact from BankGenerator.
BankAccount links bank details to account identifiers, balances, currency, and account lifecycle dates.
CreditCard links cardholder, account, and bank data with card credentials, limits, balances, and dates.
Transaction caches and claims its unique ID and records an account-linked payment event with amount, classification, merchant, status, channel, and location.
The initializer exports the four finance services that connect their respective models and generators.
BankAccountService binds its concrete generator and model and declares the entity fields exposed to the registry and DSL.
BankService binds its concrete generator and model and declares the entity fields exposed to the registry and DSL.
CreditCardService binds its concrete generator and model and declares the entity fields exposed to the registry and DSL.
TransactionService binds its concrete generator and model and declares the entity fields exposed to the registry and DSL.

components.label: models
responsibilities: Expose lazy Bank, BankAccount, CreditCard, and Transaction models, including linked account and merchant details; own the package initializer that re-exports them.
forbidden_responsibilities: Generate dataset values directly or own service orchestration.

requires.rationale: Finance entities delegate value creation and computed properties to generators.
Entity serializers return finance-owned payload contracts.

components.label: generators
responsibilities: Generate bank and account identifiers and balances, bank contact values, card credentials, status, credit limits and balances, and transactions with categorized amounts, merchants, currencies, and dates.

requires.rationale: CreditCardGenerator uses the Luhn check-digit primitive when generating card numbers.
Generator result signatures use finance-owned payload contracts.

components.label: contracts
responsibilities: Own the typed payload shapes exchanged by finance generators and models.
forbidden_responsibilities: Generate financial values or depend on finance generators, models, or services.

components.label: services
responsibilities: Bind the four finance models to their generators and publish descriptor field schemas and required datasets.
forbidden_responsibilities: Implement generator algorithms or bypass the entity models.

requires.rationale: Services return and compose finance entities.
Services instantiate the matching finance generators.

components.label: algorithms
forbidden_responsibilities: Depend on finance entities, generators, or services.

rules.rationale: Each finance implementation module has one semantic owner; the package initializer is the source module.
Entity and service dependencies are explicit while generators remain independent of entities and services.
Only entity, generator, service, finance payload contracts, and the check-digit operation cross component boundaries.
Finance ownership flows from contracts and algorithms to generators, then entities and services.
Value algorithms; must not import entity models/services. Exact reviewed target children; no hidden extra modules.
Lazy domain entities; may call generators for computed values. Exact reviewed target children; no hidden extra modules.
Domain construction workflows using models and generators. Exact reviewed target children; no hidden extra modules.
